---
id: c-m1-word-freq
title: Word Frequency Report
difficulty: Hard
order: 2
tags: dynamic memory, strings, qsort, function pointers, ctype
time_limit: 2
---
## Statement
Read an entire text from standard input (any size, up to ~10 MB) and produce a frequency report.

- A **word** is a maximal run of ASCII letters and apostrophes, **converted to lowercase**. A word must contain at least one letter, and leading/trailing apostrophes are stripped (`'tis'` → `tis`, `''` is no word). Everything else is a separator.
- Print `words N distinct D` (N = total words, D = distinct words).
- Then the **top K** words (K is the first token of the input, before the text), one per line as `COUNT WORD`, sorted by count descending, ties alphabetically ascending. Print fewer if D < K.
- Then `longest WORD` (ties → alphabetically first), or `longest -` if there are no words.

No fixed limits on word length or count: use dynamic arrays. Hash tables come later in the course, so sort-based counting (collect all words, `qsort`, count runs) is the intended approach.

## Starter
```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <ctype.h>

int main(void) {
    int k;
    if (scanf("%d", &k) != 1) return 1;
    /* read words from the rest of stdin */
    return 0;
}
```

## Hints
- Read characters with `getchar` into a growable buffer for the current word. When a separator arrives, trim apostrophes, check for a letter, and push a copy onto a growable `char **` array.
- `qsort(words, n, sizeof(char *), cmp_str)`, where `cmp_str` receives **pointers to the elements**, i.e. `char **`: `return strcmp(*(char *const *)a, *(char *const *)b);`.
- After sorting, equal words are adjacent: one pass builds an array of `(word, count)` structs, then a second `qsort` with a comparator on `(-count, word)` gives the ranking.
- With 900 000 words, keep it O(N log N). Don't search linearly for each word.

## Solution
```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <ctype.h>

typedef struct { char *w; int count; } Entry;

static void *xrealloc(void *p, size_t n) {
    void *q = realloc(p, n);
    if (!q) { perror("realloc"); exit(1); }
    return q;
}

static int cmp_str(const void *a, const void *b) {
    return strcmp(*(char *const *)a, *(char *const *)b);
}

static int cmp_entry(const void *a, const void *b) {
    const Entry *x = a, *y = b;
    if (x->count != y->count) return y->count - x->count;   /* count descending */
    return strcmp(x->w, y->w);                              /* then alphabetical */
}

int main(void) {
    int k;
    if (scanf("%d", &k) != 1) return 1;

    char **words = NULL;
    size_t n = 0, cap = 0;
    char *buf = NULL;
    size_t blen = 0, bcap = 0;
    int c;
    do {
        c = getchar();
        if (c != EOF && (isalpha(c) || c == '\'')) {
            if (blen + 1 >= bcap) { bcap = bcap ? bcap * 2 : 32; buf = xrealloc(buf, bcap); }
            buf[blen++] = (char)tolower(c);
            continue;
        }
        if (blen == 0) continue;
        size_t s = 0, e = blen;                                 /* trim apostrophes */
        while (s < e && buf[s] == '\'') s++;
        while (e > s && buf[e - 1] == '\'') e--;
        if (e > s) {                                            /* non-empty => has a letter */
            if (n == cap) { cap = cap ? cap * 2 : 1024; words = xrealloc(words, cap * sizeof *words); }
            char *w = malloc(e - s + 1);
            if (!w) { perror("malloc"); exit(1); }
            memcpy(w, buf + s, e - s);
            w[e - s] = '\0';
            words[n++] = w;
        }
        blen = 0;
    } while (c != EOF);
    free(buf);

    qsort(words, n, sizeof *words, cmp_str);
    Entry *ent = malloc((n ? n : 1) * sizeof *ent);
    size_t d = 0;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        if (d > 0 && strcmp(ent[d - 1].w, words[i]) == 0) ent[d - 1].count++;
        else ent[d++] = (Entry){words[i], 1};
    }
    printf("words %zu distinct %zu\n", n, d);

    const char *longest = NULL;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < d; i++)                           /* ent is alphabetical here */
        if (!longest || strlen(ent[i].w) > strlen(longest)) longest = ent[i].w;
    char *longest_copy = longest ? strcpy(malloc(strlen(longest) + 1), longest) : NULL;

    qsort(ent, d, sizeof *ent, cmp_entry);
    for (size_t i = 0; i < d && i < (size_t)k; i++) printf("%d %s\n", ent[i].count, ent[i].w);
    printf("longest %s\n", longest_copy ? longest_copy : "-");

    free(longest_copy);
    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; i++) free(words[i]);
    free(words);
    free(ent);
    return 0;
}
```

**Why it's built this way:**
- **Two growable arrays** (the current word's characters, and the list of words) handle input of any size with amortised O(1) appends.
- **Sort, then count runs:** sorting groups equal strings, so counting is a linear scan. That's O(N log N) overall without a hash table. The `qsort` comparator gets pointers *to the array elements*, which are `char *`, hence the `char *const *` cast, a classic source of crashes.
- **A second sort with a compound comparator** implements "count desc, then word asc". Returning `y->count - x->count` is safe here because counts are positive and far below `INT_MAX`.
- **Ownership:** `ent[i].w` *borrows* the strings owned by `words`, so each string is freed exactly once through `words`. The longest word is found while `ent` is still in alphabetical order (making the first longest the alphabetically first), then copied before re-sorting.
